articles.title: Region-specific evaluation of Hounsfield units on elbow CT as a predictor of osteoporosis in patients at risk.
articles.authors: Klingler F, Schmid C, Muhlenfeld N, Jung M, Bogner B, Knoblauch AL, et al.
articles.population: Patients at risk of osteoporosis who underwent both elbow CT scan and DXA scan within two years
articles.outcomes: Correlation between Hounsfield units on CT and DXA measurements; discriminatory capacity for osteoporosis detection using area under ROC curve
articles.take_home: Measurements of bone density on elbow CT scans correlated well with standard osteoporosis tests, with the ulnar notch and humeral capitulum showing particularly good ability to detect osteoporosis. This suggests elbow CT scans could help identify bone quality in patients before trauma surgery when formal osteoporosis testing is not available.

articles.title: Lower Postoperative Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index Is Associated with Increased Complications and Reoperations Following Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Polam V, Stokes L, Sauvanell YM, Gosselin M, Nahr A, Denard PJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anatomic or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications, reoperations, range of motion, patient-reported outcomes (ASES, VAS pain, WOOS, SANE), patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: Patients with poor nutritional status after shoulder replacement surgery (low GNRI score) had significantly higher rates of complications and reoperations, though their long-term pain relief and function were similar to well-nourished patients. Checking nutritional status before surgery may help identify patients at higher risk of problems.

articles.title: Does Teres Minor Trophicity Affect Outcomes After Arthroscopically-Assisted Lower Trapezius Tendon Transfer in Irreparable Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears?
articles.authors: Baek CH, Kim BT, Kim JG, Lim C, Kim SJ
articles.population: Patients with irreparable posterosuperior rotator cuff tears undergoing arthroscopically-assisted lower trapezius tendon transfer
articles.sample_size: 104 patients (19 hypertrophic teres minor, 72 normal, 13 hypotrophic)
articles.outcomes: Pain (Visual Analog Scale), function (Constant and ASES scores), range of motion, achievement of minimal clinically important difference, and complication rates
articles.take_home: Lower trapezius tendon transfer significantly improved pain, shoulder function, and movement in all patients regardless of teres minor muscle size before surgery. The size of the teres minor muscle did not affect how well patients recovered or their risk of retear.

articles.title: Hormone replacement therapy and complications after primary total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Ninness H, Catanzaro C, Guareschi M, Rogalski BL, Eichinger JK, Friedman RJ
articles.population: Menopausal aged women undergoing primary total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications including acute kidney injury, urinary tract infection, pneumonia, transfusion, and surgical complications
articles.take_home: Women taking hormone replacement therapy before shoulder replacement surgery had lower rates of certain medical complications such as kidney injury, pneumonia and urinary tract infections after surgery, and there was no increase in surgical complications. The study suggests HRT may have protective effects against some medical complications following this type of surgery.

articles.title: Restoring the anatomic tension relationship of the long head of the biceps during tenodesis: A prospective, randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Farooq H, Boubekri AM, Chen A, Mircoff S, Garbis NG, Scheidt M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with long head of biceps tendinopathy undergoing biceps tenodesis
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, pain scores, range of motion at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year
articles.take_home: Both standard and patient-specific tensioning techniques for biceps tenodesis produced similar pain relief and shoulder function at one year. Patient-specific tensioning showed slightly better function at 6 weeks, which may help patients wanting faster recovery.

articles.title: Bony ongrowth in stemless reverse total shoulder arthroplasty components.
articles.authors: Cardona-Perez V, Mousavi SZ, Perez-Garcia DA, Rivera AR, Ahmed A, Srikumaran U
articles.study_type: Case reports with laboratory analysis of explanted components
articles.population: Patients who had stemless reverse total shoulder arthroplasty and underwent revision surgery
articles.outcomes: Bony ongrowth on titanium-hydroxyapatite coated humeral components assessed by microscopy; osseointegration observed across all three components with no cases revised for fixation failure
articles.take_home: Bone was growing onto the surface of stemless shoulder implants, even as early as 39 days after surgery, suggesting these components may integrate well with bone. However, more research is needed to confirm these implants remain secure over many years.

articles.title: Long-term survival outcomes following total shoulder arthroplasty: An implant-level systematic review and meta-analysis of case series and registry data with more than 13 years follow-up.
articles.authors: Bhatti F, Waseem S, Singh H, Scott R, Shepherd J, Divall P, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of case series and registry data
articles.population: Patients who received anatomic or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: Data from four national joint registries and seven studies
articles.outcomes: Implant survival rates (need for revision surgery) at 13, 15, and 20 years follow-up
articles.take_home: About 90 per cent of shoulder replacements survive without needing revision surgery up to 15 years after implantation. Reverse shoulder replacements performed slightly better than standard ones in the long term.

articles.title: Traumatic Posterior Dislocation Is Associated with Posterior Acromial Morphology.
articles.authors: Werthel JD, Vervaecke A, Petit M, Jamei-Martel O, Gerber C
articles.population: Patients with first-time acute traumatic shoulder dislocation
articles.sample_size: 68 patients (34 with posterior dislocation, 34 with anterior dislocation)
articles.outcomes: Posterior acromial morphology measurements including tilt, coverage, height and critical shoulder angle
articles.take_home: People who experience a traumatic posterior shoulder dislocation tend to have a different shape at the back of their shoulder blade compared to those with anterior dislocations, with a steeper tilt and greater height at the back. This particular shoulder shape appears to make posterior dislocations more likely to occur.

articles.title: Avulsion fracture of the coracoid process at the coracoclavicular ligament attachment associated with distal clavicle fracture: A case report.
articles.authors: Yamamoto K, Minokawa S, Miyake S, Shibata T, Shibata Y, Izaki T
articles.population: 59-year-old man with distal clavicle fracture and coracoid process avulsion fracture
articles.outcomes: Fracture healing at 3 months, complete union at 6 months, full patient-reported outcome measures at 12 months
articles.take_home: A rare avulsion fracture of the coracoid process with a distal clavicle fracture was successfully treated with surgical fixation, achieving complete healing and excellent functional recovery by 12 months.

articles.title: Microfracture for glenohumeral cartilage defects: Short- to mid-term results. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Dhillon J, Bui C, Williams K, Kirby K, McCrum C, Hansen L, et al.
articles.population: Young, active patients with cartilage defects of the shoulder joint
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Score improved by 20.3 points, pain reduced by 2.2 points on Visual Analogue Scale, 20.9% required further surgery, no procedure-related complications reported
articles.take_home: Microfracture surgery for shoulder cartilage defects improves pain and function in the short to medium term and appears safe, but about one in five patients need further surgery and some show signs of ongoing arthritis despite feeling better.
